questions.question: Q1. What makes a robot a 'soft' robot?

answers.a: It is controlled by soft, user-friendly software.
answers.b: Its body deforms to move and grip instead of using rigid links and joints.
answers.c: It is quieter than a metal robot.

explanations.a: Incorrect — 'soft' refers to the mechanical body, not the software.
explanations.b: Correct — Soft robots deform their compliant bodies rather than rotating rigid joints.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Noise is not the defining property.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Payload is a consequence, not the definition.

questions.question: Q2. In Sub-Calc A, what does the drive-pressure slider P physically control?

answers.a: The gauge pressure in the eccentric air cavity that bends the finger.

explanations.a: Correct — P is the cavity gauge pressure that generates the bending moment M = P·A·d.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Friction belongs to the crawling gait in Sub-Calc C.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Temperature belongs to Sub-Calc B.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Gains are set in Sub-Calc E.

questions.question: Q3. The bending moment on the pneumatic finger is computed as:

explanations.a: Incorrect — E·I_eff is the flexural rigidity, not the moment.
explanations.b: Incorrect — This is not the moment expression used.
explanations.c: Correct — Pressure times cavity area times eccentricity gives the moment.
explanations.d: Incorrect — κ·L is the tip angle, not the moment.

questions.question: Q4. In Sub-Calc B, what happens to the shape-memory polymer's modulus when it is cooled below T_g = 40 °C?

answers.b: It jumps to a stiff glassy value (~1.5 GPa) and locks the bend.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Below T_g it is no longer rubbery.
explanations.b: Correct — Vitrification jumps E to E_passive = 1.5 GPa and freezes the shape.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Stiffness rises, it does not vanish.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Cooling vitrifies rather than melts the polymer.

questions.question: Q5. Why is the SMP-locked hold power in Sub-Calc B reported as 0 W?

answers.b: Because the sensors are turned off.
answers.d: Because once vitrified the frozen shape needs no continuous actuation to hold.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Pressure is released, not negative.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Sensing has nothing to do with the hold power.
explanations.c: Incorrect — The finger is still attached; it simply needs no power to stay bent.
explanations.d: Correct — A glassy, locked shape holds passively, unlike a leaking pneumatic hold at P·Q_leak.

questions.question: Q6. For the crawling worm in Sub-Calc C, what is the friction asymmetry μ_asym?

answers.a: The ratio μ_back / μ_fwd of backward to forward friction.
answers.b: The average of forward and backward friction.
answers.c: The friction times the actuation frequency.
answers.d: The segment strain divided by length.

explanations.a: Correct — μ_asym = μ_back/μ_fwd sets how much of each stroke becomes net travel.
explanations.b: Incorrect — It is a ratio, not an average.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Frequency sets speed, not the asymmetry.
explanations.d: Incorrect — That describes the extension stroke, not friction.

questions.question: Q7. When μ_asym = 1 on a smooth surface, what does the crawling robot do?

answers.c: Oscillates in place with zero net displacement.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Symmetric friction gives no forward drive.
explanations.c: Correct — δ_net = δ_ext·(1 − 1/1) = 0, so it just stretches and recoils in place.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The model does not predict tipping.

questions.question: Q8. In the three-finger gripper (Sub-Calc D), why does the grasp force fall to zero at a finger angle of 90°?

answers.a: Because the pressure drops to zero.
answers.d: Because F = P·A_tip·cosθ and cos(90°) = 0, so the normal force vanishes.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Pressure can be high; it is the geometry that kills the force.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Friction does not diverge here.
explanations.c: Incorrect — The object's weight is unchanged.
explanations.d: Correct — The cosθ factor sends the normal force to zero at 90°.

questions.question: Q9. What is the force-closure condition that decides whether the gripper holds an object?

answers.c: The object is smaller than the palm.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Pressure alone is not the closure test.
explanations.b: Correct — Each of the three fingers must carry a third of the weight through friction.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Size sets the workspace, not the hold condition.
explanations.d: Incorrect — There is no fixed 45° rule.

questions.question: Q10. In the PID control of Sub-Calc E, what is the tracking error e?

answers.a: The difference θ_set − y between the target angle and the current angle.

explanations.a: Correct — The controller acts on e = θ_set − y, the setpoint minus the measured angle.
explanations.b: Incorrect — That is the controller output u, not the error.
explanations.c: Incorrect — τ_p is the plant lag, not the error.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Overshoot is a response metric, not the loop error.
